Hi Alex — thanks for the runbook, looks clear. We can support the 48h window. Two straightforward approaches that would work quickly: 

1) Pay-as-you-go overrun: we lift your rate limit for the requested window and bill overrun at standard overrun rate (listed in your contract). No prep required but higher unit cost.

2) Prepaid burst credits: you purchase a block of burst credits applied to that 48h window. We can offer a one-time discount on prepaid credits for customers in pilot.

Provisional pricing options (ballpark):
- PAYG overrun: $0.024/token (short-window overrun premium)
- Prepaid burst credit: $0.018/token (20% discount off PAYG) if prepaid and invoiced before the window starts

If you can commit to a 6-month minimum commitment post-launch we can look at an extra concession on the prepaid rate (we’d need legal to add a short amendment). I’ve attached a provisional term draft for the surge window so your procurement can review.

Next steps: if you want the prepaid path, can Procurement send a PO by EOD Monday? I’ll loop in Finance and set up an invoice.

Looping in briefly. We can approve a temporary concession for pilots to protect the relationship. Proposal from Redwood (approved in principle):

- Prepaid burst credit at $0.015/token (25% off the initial PAYG ask) if BrightCart prepays for the burst block by Monday EOD.
- Commercial commitment: BrightCart signs a 6-month minimum post-launch at existing committed tiers (not a full enterprise commit) — this unlocks the 25% concession.
- Cap: we will guarantee a billing cap such that the effective per-token charge during the window will not exceed 1.5x your baseline ARR rate. This cap only applies to billable burst tokens (not to any separate premium routing or add-ons).
- Payment split recommendation: 50% prepaid burst credits + 50% PAYG buffer (to handle unpredictable tail usage). We will reconcile and true-up after the window.

Laura — can you confirm we can invoice under the same small-business PO flow if procurement sends PO #? Also confirm that Finance will accept the 50/50 split and handle a retroactive true-up.

Jonas
